fields.title: Financial plan: how much runway you have
fields.keyTakeaway: Product strategy decisions require three figures: current cash balance, monthly burn rate, and runway in months. They anchor roadmap debates in timeline constraints.
fields.checkQuestion: The team asks for six months to build a new business line. What three numbers do you need before answering?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **how will financial goals be achieved?**
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you do not answer the question.** Strategic plans assume infinite runway. Then reality strikes with five months of cash remaining, forcing panicky, flawed operational trade-offs.
fields.blocks/2/title: Three metrics every product manager must track
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: They should be reviewed with the CFO quarterly
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Cash reserve** — available balance plus confirmed incoming payments.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Burn rate** — net monthly spend in excess of revenue.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Runway in months** — cash balance divided by burn rate. Defines the timeframe within which roadmap bets must pay off.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Plus two qualifiers:** burn rate levers (costs that can be cut quickly) and revenue risks (unconfirmed pipeline).
fields.blocks/3/text: **This yields a clear prioritization rule.** If runway is under 12 months, do not launch initiatives with payback horizons exceeding that window — not because they are bad ideas, but because cash will run out before impact materializes.
fields.blocks/4/text:
Cash balance: 18 million ₽. Monthly net burn: 2.1 million ₽. Remaining runway: 8.5 months.

Proposed initiative: custom manufacturing vertical, projected payback of 14 months.

Verdict: not "bad idea", but "unaffordable given our current runway". Shifted focus to regulatory compliance (8-week dev effort, mandated for 40% of clients) and a 15% price bump for new acquisitions.

Two quarters later, net monthly burn dropped to 0.4 million ₽, extending runway to over two years — enabling the board to revisit the new vertical.

The same three metrics clearly demonstrated to the board why the rejection was a matter of timing, not merit.
fields.blocks/5/text: Calculate runway conservatively: ignore pipeline deals until signed. Strategic roadmaps built on "imminent contract closes" invariably fail when those deals delay.
fields.blocks/5/title: Revenue projections are the most optimistic part of any plan
fields.blocks/6/text: A financial plan does not dictate product strategy — it establishes boundaries on what is feasible. Within those boundaries, product decisions remain driven by customer value and strategy.
